items.label: E1
items.text:
Saplings in the fixture orchard are planted between the third and fifth week of the planting season. Each sapling receives 12 litres of water on the day it is planted.

Approved sapling varieties:

1. Red Fixture Apple

2. Golden Fixture Pear

3. Blue Fixture Plum

items.label: E2
items.text: Pruning happens once per year after the last frost. Branches thicker than a thumb are cut with a saw, never with shears.

items.label: E3
items.text:
FIXTURE ORCHARD HANDBOOK
TEST FIXTURE ONLY. Synthetic text written for software tests; it is not part of any real corpus.

items.label: E4
items.text: Ladders are not permitted in the orchard overnight and must be returned to the tool shed.

items.label: E5
items.text: Wicks are trimmed to a height of 4 millimetres. A wick trimmed too short produces a dim beam; a wick left too long produces soot on the lens.

items.label: E6
items.text: A picker may fill at most 40 crates per shift. Damaged fruit is placed in the compost bin, not in the crates. The harvest supervisor checks the crate count at the end of every shift. Crates are stacked no more than five high. Stacks taller than five crates must be split before the cart leaves the row. The cart driver confirms the stack height before moving. Fruit picked after sunset is recorded separately. Late fruit is stored in the cool room until the next morning.

items.label: E7
items.text: Ladders are permitted in the orchard only when a second worker holds the base of the ladder.
